title: Frequently Asked Questions About Small Business, 2023

facts.fact: Small businesses account for 99.9% of American businesses, per SBA Office of Advocacy's 2023 FAQ.
facts.quote: Most businesses are small- 99.9% of American businesses.

facts.fact: There are 33,185,550 small businesses in the United States, per SBA Office of Advocacy's 2023 FAQ.
facts.quote: There are 33,185,550 small businesses in the United States.

facts.fact: Small businesses employ 61.7 million Americans, totaling 46.4% of private sector employees.
facts.quote: Small businesses employ 61.7 million Americans, totaling 46.4% of private sector employees.

facts.fact: From 1995 to 2021, small businesses created 17.3 million net new jobs.
facts.quote: From 1995 to 2021, small businesses created 17.3 million net new jobs, accounting for 62.7% of net jobs created since 1995.

facts.fact: Small businesses pay 39.4% of private sector payroll.
facts.quote: Small businesses pay 39.4% percent of private sector payroll.

facts.fact: Small businesses generate 32.6% of known export value.
facts.quote: Small businesses generate 32.6% percent of known export value.

facts.fact: About 38% of small businesses use specialized software in their business operations.
facts.quote: About 38% of small businesses use specialized software in their business operations.

facts.fact: The SBA Office of Advocacy generally defines a small business as an independent business having fewer than 500 employees.
facts.quote: Advocacy generally defines a small business as an independent business having fewer than 500 employees.

facts.fact: The SBA Office of Advocacy supports businesses with fewer than 500 employees, non-profit organizations, and independent contractors.
facts.quote: The Office of Advocacy supports businesses with fewer than 500 employees, non-profit organizations, and independent contractors.

facts.fact: The SBA Office of Advocacy does not take part in SBA's work on loans, disaster relief, or procurement.
facts.quote: We do not take part in SBA’s work on loans, disaster relief, or procurement.
